title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): X' is a conformal (Riemann) surface, a is a point of X', and D ⊂ Int(X') is a compact closed conformal disk containing a, with rectifiable boundary. The tangent line T_{X',a} carries only an infinitesimal conformal structure: it is a complex line up to similarity. In such a line the round disks centred at 0 form a torsor under R*_{>0} acting by homotheties.

1. The 'shadow' map. The page opens with the map D ↦ o(D), the 'ombre de D'. Let f : (D,a) → (unit disk, 0) be the Riemann map, unique up to rotation. Its differential df_a : T_{X',a} → C is then defined up to a unit complex number. So o(D) := (df_a)^{-1}(unit disk) is a well-defined round disk in T_{X',a}. Its radius is the conformal radius of D at a, measured in the conformal structure of T_{X',a}. Equivalently, o(D) records the reduced module of D minus a, i.e. the 1-jet of the uniformizing coordinate modulo rotation.

2. Two remarks Grothendieck makes.
(i) The map D ↦ o(D) has no reason to be injective. Many disks around a have the same conformal radius.
(ii) Concentric disks behave well. For λ ∈ ]0,1], let D_λ = f^{-1}(|z| ≤ λ). Then o(D_λ) = λ·o(D). So D ↦ o(D) is equivariant for the monoid ]0,1] of contracting homotheties. The family {D_λ} is the canonical 'concentric' family attached to D.

3. The case he says he is really interested in. X' is compact with a finite family of marked points (a_i)_{i∈I}. One takes mutually disjoint disks D_i around the a_i, which give a system of shadows o(D_i) ⊂ T_{X',a_i}. He then asks for finer restrictive conditions on the system of D_i that would imply ('qui sait?') that the system is determined by the system of its shadows. In other words, he looks for a canonical section 'shadows → disks' of a map that is not injective in general.

4. Where this goes next (following page). He passes to X* = X minus the open disks, with the canonical constant-curvature metric (geodesic boundary in the hyperbolic cases). Each ∂D_i then carries two 'toric' (circle-torsor) structures, one from D_i and one from X*. He proposes to require that these two structures coincide.

5. What it serves. This is the 'surgery of conformal surfaces' programme of 1983–84: cutting and pasting Riemann surfaces along disks and circles, in the context of the Teichmüller tower of the Esquisse. The page tries to replace the infinite-dimensional datum 'disjoint disks around punctures' by the finite-dimensional datum 'tangent vectors / conformal radii at punctures' via a canonical normalisation of the disks. This is the same problem later met in conformal field theory: surfaces with parametrised boundary versus surfaces with punctures and local coordinates or tangent vectors.
errors: No mathematical errors. The non-injectivity remark and the ]0,1]-equivariance are correct.

Implicit gap: for a given system of shadows there may be no system of pairwise disjoint disks realising it at all (shadows too large), or infinitely many (shadows small). By the ]0,1]-equivariance, any realisable system yields realisations of every smaller system λ_i·o(D_i). So uniqueness genuinely needs a 'maximality/filling' type condition. Grothendieck flags this only as an open question.

Classical extremal-length theory (Jenkins, Strebel) answers a closely related question. Disjoint disks maximising a weighted sum of reduced moduli exist and are unique, given by Jenkins–Strebel quadratic differentials with double poles at the a_i, and their closures fill X. This suggests the 'restrictive conditions' should be of extremal/filling type. The page does not note this.

ideas.what: Shadow o(D) of a conformal disk around a point: the round disk in T_{X,a} given by the conformal radius / 1-jet of the Riemann map modulo rotation
ideas.modern_name: conformal radius / reduced module; 1-jet of local uniformizing coordinate (tangent vector up to rotation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Riemann mapping theorem, Teichmüller/Grötzsch reduced module, Jenkins)

ideas.what: Equivariance of D ↦ o(D) for the monoid ]0,1] of contracting homotheties via concentric sub-disks
ideas.modern_name: action of the semigroup of standard annuli / contraction semigroup; shrinking of local coordinates
ideas.usually_credited_to: Segal (semigroup of annuli, CFT definition, c.1987); Huang (spheres with tubes, VOA geometry, 1990s)

ideas.what: Problem: on a compact Riemann surface with marked points, find natural conditions on a system of disjoint disks around the points making it determined by its system of shadows (tangent data)
ideas.modern_name: canonical disk/coordinate systems from tangent data; Jenkins–Strebel extremal configurations; comparison of moduli of surfaces with parametrised boundary versus punctures with tangent vectors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jenkins (1950s), Strebel (Quadratic Differentials, 1984); in the CFT setting Segal, Vafa, Friedan–Shenker, Huang

missed.claim: In 1983–84 Grothendieck sets up, in conformal-geometric language, the comparison between Riemann surfaces with marked points and disjoint disks (boundary parametrisations) and surfaces with marked points and tangent data. This includes the monoid ]0,1] of concentric shrinkings. These are the ingredients of Segal's sewing formalism for CFT (1987) and Huang's geometric VOA theory, which he does not seem to be credited with.
missed.quote: D → o(D) est compatible aux homothéties de rapport λ ∈ ]0,1]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents an independent early appearance of the 'semigroup of annuli / surgery of Riemann surfaces' viewpoint, linked to his Teichmüller-tower programme rather than to physics.

missed.claim: Open question: which natural conditions on a system of disjoint disks around marked points make it uniquely determined by its shadows? The next page proposes matching of the two circle structures on each ∂D_i, one from D_i and one from the hyperbolic X*. This is a canonical-section problem not obviously treated in the literature in this form. Jenkins–Strebel gives one answer for the extremal/filling variant, but the 'matching toric structures' condition looks unexplored.
missed.quote: On demande des conditions restrictives plus fines sur le système des D_i, impliquant (qui sait?) qu'il soit déterminé par le système des ombres.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A canonical 'shadows → disks' section would give a canonical splitting between the moduli of punctured surfaces with tangent vectors and the moduli with boundary parametrisations. It might also relate to hyperbolic decompositions of the Penner/Bowditch–Epstein type.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is elementary: conformal radius and equivariance under shrinking. The interest lies in the early (1983–84) formulation of a surgery/sewing framework for conformal surfaces close to Segal's later CFT formalism, and in a clearly posed but unresolved canonical-disk problem. It is not a finished new result.

'les disques conformes contenus [?] D s. [?] ombre' likely reads 'les disques conformes centrés [en a] de même ombre dans T_{X';a}'.
'Je m'intéresse au fait [?] au cas' should be 'Je m'intéresse en fait au cas'.
'Une demande des conditions restrictives' should be 'On demande des conditions restrictives'.
'sur [?] la répartition des D_i' should be 'sur le système des D_i'.
'qu'il est déterminé par la symétrie [?] des ombres' should be 'qu'il est (soit) déterminé par le système des ombres'.
'donnant [?] les λ o(D)' and 'donnant [?] des ombres' likely read 'donnant'/'définissant'. The illegible word before 'λ ∈ ]0,1]' is crossed out.
